doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Rights, residuals and distribution
summary: Crohn explains selling regional rights to History of Jazz, BBC and Bravo payments, and uncertain web distribution.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How do you get included in getting those residuals or whatever. Is that something that you have in a contract?

No that depends. Like when I did the film for Hamilton College, there was nothing. You hired me as the director and producer and I did it. When I first did the “History of Jazz” series, we basically sold it off. Like when we got money from Japan they got Japanese rights and that’s all they got. And they could screen it in Japan, but then we had the rights to sell it in other parts of the world. The “History of Jazz” series I did has been seen in something like forty countries around the world. And the BBC, back then they paid big money for jazz films, I mean twenty, twenty-five thousand dollars. I was on BRAVO, I think they paid ten, eleven thousand dollars. It adds up. But we kept the rights to sell it in different places. I look at the distribution now, it’s very high. Distribution is changing all the time. You can distribute on the net. You have webcasts, you do — maybe you have to put up a site, I don’t even know how I’m going to distribute this film.
